diagnosis_in_five_lines: E3 dialogue was written to be scored, not spoken: each line was manufactured to satisfy a named gate requirement, with the requirement printed beside the line in the script.
The gates then read the script back in the same vocabulary and certified it — Gate E's questions are answered BETTER by ledger lines, so the gate selects for reportage.

Result: wants announced in 'I want X' form, rules recited whole, claims reported to rooms containing the people they concern, bookend restatements closing mandated pairs — 21 E3 lines contain zero questions between characters, zero interruptions, zero wrong answers.

The repair gradient made it worse: hear-before-it-moves measured parse, not plausibility, and its emblematic fix formalized the contraction 'Thirty's' into 'Thirty is' — the gate edited spokenness out.
No gate ever asked the user's question — would a person say that line, to that person, there? — so the new Stranger Test asks exactly that, on dialogue alone, annotations stripped.
